name: sURL-3K and OADS-1K
description: Authors routinely point to the datasets and software their studies use through URLs in their papers, which we call OADS-URLs. Many no longer lead to the resource they point to. How much of the cited open access datasets and software (OADS) is still reachable is not well understood, leaving web archives no basis for deciding which endangered resources to preserve first. My dissertation measures the availability and discoverability of OADS-URLs at scale and how fast they decline. We built two benchmarks, sURL-3K and OADS-1K. On sURL-3K we evaluated our proposed extraction method, VisURLX, against heuristic baselines. VisURLX reads rendered page images with a multimodal large language model and is the most accurate, at an F1 score of 86.86%. On OADS-1K we developed EnSU, which classifies each URL by resource type and provider at a macro F1 of 90%. With the pipeline that best trades accuracy against cost and EnSU, we will build OADS Repo from about 16 million scholarly documents and measure how availability and discoverability differ across discipline, provider, host, venue, and institution, and how fast OADS-URLs disappear. The results will show how much of the endangered record can be preserved and which OADS to capture first.
